x: C is correct: the first launch pad at Sriharikota handles PSLV and SSLV. A and B swap the pads (the second pad handles GSLV and LVM3 and is standby for PSLV). D is wrong: PSLV-C62 flew from the first launch pad; the Third Launch Pad is still to be built for NGLV.

D is the mismatch: Sarabhai was the first ISRO Chairman until his death in 1971, founded PRL and is called the Father of the Indian space programme. The Indian Deep Space Network at Byalalu near Bengaluru is not among his foundations (PRL, IIM Ahmedabad, Darpana Academy, ATIRA).
All three statements are correct: the Kulasekarapattinam complex is mainly for SSLV launches as private players enter the sector, and it is in Thoothukudi (Tuticorin) district of Tamil Nadu.

D is correct: GSAT-11 (2018), about 5.8 tonnes, is the heaviest ISRO-built communication satellite and serves high-speed internet and rural broadband. A describes GSAT-7 'Rukmini' (Navy, 2013), B describes INSAT-1B (system commissioned 1983) and C describes GSAT-6 (2015).
